cards.back: Retrieval is tuned for recall and casts a wide net quickly. Reranking is tuned for precision and puts the best few candidates on top.
The prompt only holds a handful of chunks and models pay most attention to the first ones, so reordering is often the cheapest quality win in RAG.
Embeds query and chunk separately into vectors compared by cosine or dot product. The corpus is precomputed, so search takes milliseconds.
Reads query and chunk concatenated and outputs one relevance score. Tokens interact, so it catches what similarity misses, but it runs once per candidate.

cards.front: Why not cross-encode the whole corpus?
cards.back: The score depends on the query, so nothing can be precomputed: 50,000 chunks would mean 50,000 transformer passes per query.
rerank_ms ≈ candidates × (tokens_per_pair / 512) ÷ pairs_per_second_at_512 × 1000. It sits on the critical path before the LLM starts.
Measure first-stage recall@k. If recall@50 is about the same as recall@100, send 50.
No. A cross-encoder outputs a raw logit trained to order chunks for one query, so pick any threshold on your own labelled set.
Keeps one small vector per token. Each query token finds its best-matching chunk token (MaxSim) and the score is the sum, without a transformer pass per pair.
Training negatives the retriever ranked highly but are wrong. Random negatives teach a reranker nothing.

cards.front: Proving a reranker earns its latency
cards.back: Run the golden set with and without it and compare NDCG@10 and MRR. Also log first-stage recall@k.

quiz.q: Why is a cross-encoder more accurate than a bi-encoder?
choices: It searches with HNSW instead of IVF
It never compresses the chunk before seeing the question
It uses a larger embedding dimension
quiz.why: A bi-encoder must decide what a chunk is about without knowing the question; a cross-encoder reads both together.

quiz.q: The right chunk is not in the top 100 candidates. Will a better reranker fix it?
choices: Yes, with a lower score threshold
Yes, if it is a cross-encoder
Yes, if you use an LLM reranker
quiz.why: No reranker can rescue a chunk that isn't in the candidates.

quiz.q: Which change does NOT cut reranker latency?
choices: Reranking the full parent section instead of the chunk
Sending fewer candidates where recall flattens
quiz.why: Longer pairs cost more; rerank the chunk and truncate to the model's trained length.

quiz.q: What can an LLM reranker do that a cross-encoder can't?
quiz.why: LLM rerankers are instruction-following but cost 10 to 100× the latency.

quiz.q: Which listwise LLM reranking approach slides a window over 100 passages?
quiz.why: RankGPT shows ~20 passages, asks for ranked IDs and slides the window.

quiz.q: When is it reasonable to skip reranking?
choices: Exact ID lookups with only one right answer
Whenever the corpus has more than 1M chunks
quiz.why: Also skip it for tiny corpora already right on the golden set, or strict latency budgets.
